description: Grilled Sea Bass, known as Levrek in Turkey, is a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, celebrated for its delicate flavor and tender, flaky texture. This traditional recipe highlights the fish's natural taste with a simple yet aromatic marinade of olive oil, lemon, and fresh herbs, making it a healthy and incredibly satisfying meal. Perfect for a warm evening, it brings the vibrant flavors of the Turkish coast right to your table.

ingredients.notes: about 1-1.5 lbs each, cleaned and scaled with gills removed
1 sliced for stuffing, 1 for juice and wedges
optional, for a hint of spice

instructions.title: Prepare the Sea Bass
instructions.text: Rinse the cleaned sea bass under cold water, inside and out. Pat them thoroughly dry with paper towels. Make 2-3 shallow diagonal slits on both sides of each fish, being careful not to cut too deep.

instructions.title: Create the Marinade
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, juice from one lemon, minced garlic, chopped parsley, chopped dill, salt, black pepper, and dried oregano. If using, add red pepper flakes.

instructions.title: Marinate the Fish
instructions.text: Generously rub the marinade all over each sea bass, ensuring it gets into the slits and inside the cavity. Place a few lemon slices and a sprig of fresh parsley or dill into the cavity of each fish. Let them marinate at room temperature for at least 20 minutes, or refrigerate for up to 1 hour.

instructions.title: Preheat the Grill
instructions.text: Preheat your grill to medium-high heat (around 400-450F or 200-230C). Lightly oil the grill grates to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Sea Bass
instructions.text: Place the marinated sea bass directly on the hot grill. Grill for 7-10 minutes per side, depending on the thickness of the fish. The fish is done when the skin is crispy and slightly charred, and the flesh is opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Avoid overcooking.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully remove the grilled sea bass from the grill. Let them rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges and extra chopped parsley or dill. Serve immediately with a fresh green salad or roasted vegetables.

tips: For the best flavor, use fresh, wild-caught sea bass. Ask your fishmonger to clean and scale the fish for you for convenience.
Don't overcrowd the grill; cook the fish in batches if necessary to maintain consistent heat and achieve a good sear.
A fish grilling basket can be very helpful to prevent the fish from sticking or breaking apart when flipping, especially for whole fish.
